You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: 🔥 Bitget US Stock Hotspot Sniper｜2026.07.17

TEXT:
Main Theme: AI Model Competition and Hardware/Equipment Expansion in Parallel｜Google Gemini Delay· Apple iPad mini OLED Update·Hanmi Semiconductor Equipment Expansion
1. Google Gemini 3.5 Pro Launch Delayed, Sparking AI Competitiveness Concerns
Media reports indicate Google’s flagship AI model Gemini 3.5 Pro has fallen several months behind schedule, mainly because its technical performance failed to meet targets, particularly in code programming capabilities. The market is concerned that Google may lose ground as Anthropic and OpenAI continue releasing stronger models. Impacted by the news, Google shares fell more than 4.4%.
🎯 Beneficiary Tickers: GOOG ; Key Catalyst: Short-term sen time nt pressure from slower-than-expected large model iteration, while AI infrastructure and compute demand fundamentals remain intact; monitor follow-up model release pace.
2. Apple OLED iPad mini Expected to Launch This Fall
According to Bloomberg sources, Apple’s new iPad mini will feature an OLED display for the first time and is expected to launch as early as this fall, with sales targeted for around October. This marks the first major redesign and screen technology upgrade for iPad mini since 2021, which could further solidify the recovery of Apple’s iPad business. iPad revenue is projected to grow 6% this fiscal year to nearly $30 billion.
🎯 Beneficiary Tickers: AAPL ; Key Catalyst: Hardware product line refresh with OLED and potential on-device AI capabilities, supporting consumer electronics recovery and Apple’s AI ecosystem narrative.
3. Hanmi Semiconductor Plans New AI Semiconductor Equipment Factory
Hanmi Semiconductor’s chairman stated that, anticipating a supply shortage of AI semiconductor equipment starting next year, the company is considering building an eighth factory (its largest to date) adjacent to the seventh factory currently under construction. It also plans to establish a U.S. subsidiary in San Jose, California by the end of 2026 to strengthen technical support for American fabs and hyperscalers. Demand for its thermal compression bonders and hybrid bonders (key HBM packaging equipment) is expected to grow rapidly. 🎯 Beneficiary Tickers: NVDA , TSM ; Key Catalyst: Expansion of AI HBM memory packaging equipment capacity directly supports advanced AI chip production ramp-up and helps ease supply chain bottlenecks.
4. Microsoft Developing AI-Powered Vulnerability Detection and Repair Tool
According to The Information, Microsoft is preparing an AI vulnerability detection tool similar to Mythos. The new product will leverage multiple AI models to automatically scan for software vulnerabilities and complete corresponding security fixes. This aims to enhance software development security efficiency and enterprise-grade AI application deployment.
🎯 Beneficiary Tickers: MSFT ; Key Catalyst: Practical application of agentic AI tools in software security and developer productivity, strengthening Microsoft’s enterprise AI ecosystem competitiveness and monetization potential.
5. Netflix Q3 Revenue Growth Expected to Hit Near Three-Year Low
Netflix reported Q2 results that were largely in line with expectations, but guided Q3 revenue growth of only 11.7% — the lowest year-over-year pace since late 2023 — raising investor concerns about growth peaking. The stock fell more than 8% in after-hours trading. Q2 revenue reached $12.56 billion (+13% YoY) and net profit rose nearly 9% to $3.4 billion.
🎯 Beneficiary Tickers: NFLX ; Key Catalyst: Growth slowdown signal may increase market scrutiny on high-valuation growth stocks amid heavy AI capex, with focus on subscription and advertising business follow-through.
Trading Tip: Today’s individual stock hotspots center on AI model progress alongside hardware and equipment supply chain expansion. Google’s delay brings short-term sentiment pressure, while Apple’s product update and Hanmi’s equipment expansion provide positive catalysts. Microsoft’s AI tool development strengthens the application narrative, and Netflix’s slower growth guidance reflects high-valuation concerns. Focus on news flow around GOOG, AAPL, and NVDA supply chain names, and manage positions according to broader market volume and VIX.
U.S. stocks have seen heightened volatility recently. The above content is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice.
